faqs.q: Why is my competitor outranking me in France?
faqs.a: Usually it comes down to three things: stronger reviews in French, better local relevance on their pages, or more links from French sites. I audit all three before recommending anything, because the fix is different in each case. Most of the time it is not one big thing, it is ten small things done consistently.

faqs.q: Do I need a Google Business Profile in France?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free, and for local searches it often appears before any website does. French customers read the avis section closely, so a complete profile with fresh reviews in French will beat a nicer website with an empty profile. I set these up and manage them as part of every engagement.

faqs.q: Is an English-only website enough to rank in France?
faqs.a: No. The overwhelming majority of local searches in France happen in French, and Google.fr rewards pages written naturally in the searcher's language. Machine-translated pages read badly and convert worse. If you want French customers, your key pages need to be written in real French.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take to work in France?
faqs.a: Most businesses see early movement in 2 to 3 months and meaningful results in 4 to 6 months of consistent work. Competitive Paris searches take longer than a quieter regional market. Anyone promising page one in 30 days is selling you something you do not want.

faqs.q: How much should a business in France budget for SEO?
faqs.a: It depends on your city and competition, but serious local SEO is a monthly commitment, not a one-off project. Underinvesting usually costs more in lost customers than the SEO itself. My pricing is public on this site, and every engagement starts with a free audit so you know exactly what the money does.
